chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the mu‘tamir enters Makkah without tamattu‘, performs tawaf of the House, prays two rak‘ahs at the Maqām of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and performs sa‘y between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then he may return to his family if he wishes.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two hills of sa‘y
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other hill of sa‘y
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Ka‘bah, around which tawaf is performed
key_terms.تَمَتُّعٍ: the form of pilgrimage combining ‘umrah with hajj in a specified manner
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the Station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام near the Ka‘bah

ai.seo_question: After completing a non-tamattu‘ ‘umrah, may a pilgrim leave Makkah and return home?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the rites of an ‘umrah performed without the intention of tamattu‘. It states that after completing the essential rites of tawaf, the two rak‘ahs at Maqām Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and sa‘y between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, the mu‘tamir may depart and return to his family if he wishes.
